title: Incident Management, Reporting and Supervisory Intervention
summary: How firms detect, contain and recover from major operational and cyber incidents, what incident reporting should tell the authority, and how supervisors intervene without obstructing recovery.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How firms detect, contain and recover from major operational and cyber incidents, what incident reporting should tell the authority, and how supervisors intervene without obstructing recovery.
Learning Objectives: Assess the adequacy of a firm's incident response and recovery procedures
Evaluate incident reports and notifications for completeness and timeliness
Apply proportionate supervisory intervention during a live incident
Syllabus: Incident response phases: detection, containment, eradication and recovery
Incident classification, reporting thresholds and root-cause analysis
Recovery time objectives, backups and data restoration
Simulation: supervisory response to a ransomware incident
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors assessing operational resilience, ICT and cyber risk across banking, insurance, investment, payments and market infrastructure
Technology risk, cyber and outsourcing specialists supporting supervisory teams
Policy staff and senior managers shaping the authority's resilience, cyber and critical third-party approach
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision or operational risk is helpful. No technical background in IT or cybersecurity is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Operational Resilience (2021)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)
